bullets.body: **White House frontier-model pre-release vetting EO advances to interagency draft (May 6-7) — following the May 4-5 NYT scoop, senior White House officials circulate an interagency draft executive order to OSTP, NSC, NIST, and the Department of Commerce; the draft proposes a Frontier Model Review Board (FMRB) chaired jointly by NIST + ODNI cyber lead, with mandatory pre-release notification 30 days before any model surpassing offensive-cyber TLO-step thresholds (mapped to the AISI 32-step "The Last Ones" range that GPT-5.5 + Mythos already breached); the EO would lean on Defense Production Act §708 voluntary information-sharing authority rather than new statutory rulemaking, sidestepping APA notice-and-comment; Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI, and Meta were briefed on the FMRB structure last week; AI Policy Institute + R Street + AI Now flag the lack of a public-comment window as a litigation vector** — Concrete legal-vehicle disclosure (DPA §708 vs new rulemaking) is the first sign the EO trail is shipping; sets the comment-window battle for Q3 2026.

bullets.body: **EU AI Office + UK AISI publish joint cyber-eval reciprocity protocol (May 7) — European Commission AI Office and UK AI Safety Institute publish a joint memorandum-of-cooperation establishing reciprocal recognition of cyber-capability evaluations conducted under the AI Act §51 systemic-risk regime and AISI's voluntary frontier-model program; under the protocol an AISI-administered TLO-range run satisfies AI Act systemic-risk pre-deployment evaluation requirements for the same model when conducted within 90 days of EU placement; the joint protocol is timed to the White House FMRB draft and explicitly anticipates a US-side counter-protocol; Mistral, Aleph Alpha, Anthropic, and OpenAI are signed up as the initial cohort with results sharing-in-confidence to both regulators** — First multilateral cyber-eval reciprocity primitive lands; pairs with the FMRB draft to define the trans-Atlantic frontier-model regulatory shape.
